abstract: Current implementations of low-latency adaptive streaming over HTTP utilize a diversity of presentation formats, containers, origins, and caching behaviors. For efficient delivery, a common origin and a single set of cacheable media objects provide the highest performance and scalability across a delivery system. This article introduces a means of leveraging the Common Media Application Format (CMAF) as a standardized container format, combined with specific content encoding constraints and addressing mode constraints in low-latency HTTP Live Streaming (HLS) (LL-HLS) and low-latency Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH) (LL-DASH), to provide a cross-format solution that maximizes edge cache efficiency and minimizes origin storage costs and client request rate.

authors.bio: Will Law is a chief architect with the Edge Technology Group, Akamai, Cambridge, MA, and a leading media delivery technologist. Involved with streaming media on the internet for the last 21 years, he has a strong focus on client-side development and wrote many of the early connection frameworks. Currently focusing on low-latency streaming, Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG) Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH), technology evaluation, Common Media Client Data (CMCD), Common Media Application Format (CMAF), and WebTransport. Law is currently the Co-Chair of the W3C WebTransport Working Group and the Consumer Technology Association (CTA) Common Media Server Data Working Group and past Chairman of the DASH Industry Forum and the CTA Web Application Video Ecosystem (WAVE) Project. He holds a master’s degree in aerospace engineering and an MBA and has worked previously for Adobe, Internap, and a series of five engineering and media-related startups.
authors.name: Will Law

authors.bio: Eric Toullec is an advanced research engineer within Ateme’s Research and Innovation Team, Rennes, France, in which he took part in several French collaborative projects to study and promote innovative technologies. His research and development work mainly focuses on video packaging and distribution technologies. In the last four years, he was mainly working on NextGen TV technologies, and more specifically on the development, testing, and deployment of Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC) 3.0. He is currently following 5G standardization and he participates in projects taking advantage of this new technology. He is the author of several conference papers and journal articles, as well as patents. He received a PhD degree in computing science in 2005 from Rennes 1 University, Rennes.
authors.name: Eric Toullec

authors.bio: Mickaël Raulet is CTO at Ateme, where he drives research and innovation with various collaborative research and development projects. He represents Ateme in several standardization bodies: Advanced Television Systems Committee (ATSC), Digital Video Broadcasting (DVB), 3rd Generation Partnership Project (3GPP), International Organization for Standardization/International Electrotechnical Commission (ISO/IEC), International Telecommunication Union (ITU), Motion Picture Experts Group (MPEG), Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP (DASH)-IF, Common Media Application Format (CMAF)-IF, Streaming Video Alliance (SVA), and UHD Forum. He is the author of numerous patents and more than 100 conference papers and journal scientific articles. In 2006, he received a PhD degree from INSA, Rennes, France, in electronic and signal processing, in collaboration with Mitsubishi Electric ITE, Rennes.
authors.name: Mickaël Raulet
